newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav July inflation up 0.1pct m/m, 14.6pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav July inflation up 0.1pct m/m, 14.6pct y/y.

text.p: The Federal Statistics Office reported the following Yugoslav economic indicator details.
NOTES -- July retail prices were 3.3 percent up on December last year and 18.1 percent above the average for 1996.
Cumulative January-July RPI index rose 24.3 percent against the same seven-month period last year and 17.6 percent on the 1996 average.
Prices of agricultural products registered a seasonal drop on average of 0.9 percent and industrial non-food products of 0.2 percent.
Prices of industrial food products rose 0.1 percent, drinks 0.1 percent and services 0.8 percent.

Services prices were pushed up by higher car insurance and entertainment costs while prices of tobacco remained unchanged, Tanjug news agency quoted Federal Statistics Office assistant director Mirjana Rankovic as saying.
Figures refer to Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
